description: Welcome to SPACE SECURITY! Engineered by a solo systems architect from Karaganda for the 2026 NASA Space Apps "Flame in Freefall" challenge. I built IGNIS-0: an interactive Super Intelligence (SI) fire safety dashboard and 0g spherical combustion simulator powered by NASA PSI (BASS-II, Saffire, SOFIE) and partner data (JAXA, ESA, ISRO). Our mission is protecting astronaut safety across Low Earth Orbit, Artemis lunar cabins, and Mars.
summary: IGNIS-0 by SPACE SECURITY is an interactive Super Intelligence (SI) decision-support dashboard and 0g spherical combustion simulator built for the "Flame in Freefall" challenge. Developed by a solo systems architect, the platform harmonizes NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) records (BASS-II, Saffire I–VI, SOFIE) with JAXA, ESA, and ISRO partner data. IGNIS-0 predicts how spacecraft materials ignite across ISS (21% O2), Artemis Lunar (34% O2), and Mars Transit atmospheres, empowering mission designers and astronauts to prevent catastrophic deep-space fires.
details:
WHAT IT DOES:

In microgravity (0g), thermal buoyancy disappears—flames form spherical diffusion fronts driven entirely by spacecraft HVAC ventilation and behave radically differently than on Earth. IGNIS-0 unifies fragmented microgravity combustion datasets into an intuitive visual dashboard that ranks spacecraft materials by their 0g fire risk, simulates spherical flame spread rates in real time, and outputs actionable fire-suppression protocols.

HOW IT WORKS:

Users select a spacecraft cabin preset (ISS 21% O2, Artemis Lunar Lander 34% O2, or Mars Transit Habitat 26% O2) or adjust live sliders for Oxygen Concentration (% O2), Cabin Pressure (kPa), and Ventilation Airflow (cm/s). The physics engine computes non-linear opposed-flow flame spread and demonstrates how materials that self-extinguish on the ISS (such as Nomex HT90-40 at 21% O2) cross their Minimum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) threshold and become critical fire hazards in Artemis lunar atmospheres (34% O2, 56.5 kPa). It also demonstrates diffusive self-extinguishment when cabin airflow drops below 0.8 cm/s.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT:

IGNIS-0 bridges the gap between raw NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) experimental archives and practical spacecraft engineering. It helps mission designers screen materials under NASA-STD-6001B before flight and provides astronauts with rapid emergency ventilation-shutdown checklists.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOLO EXECUTION:

Conceived and engineered by a solo participant (Team SPACE SECURITY) using React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide/Feather Line Icons, and HTML5 Canvas 2D physics rendering. Designed in strict compliance with the 2026 NASA Space Apps Brand Guidelines (45-degree Electric-to-Deep Blue gradient, WCAG 2.0 AAA >15:1 contrast, and Fira Sans / Overpass / Fira Code typography).

TRANSPARENT USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI):

Core physical equations, system architecture, and dataset harmonization were 100% human-engineered. Super Intelligence (SI) tools (Gemini / Claude / Cursor) were used to accelerate TypeScript code generation, multi-variable risk score interpolation, and creation of the "SPACE SECURITY" team emblem (which carries a visible AI watermark in the bottom-right corner and explicit SI metadata in code and exported JSON reports). No official NASA agency logos were used or modified.
